meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Ethylene loss up with TIC-107 on set point (RF-CAS-v1 cascade refrigeration)
meta.caseTitle: Ethylene loss up with TIC-107 on set point
meta.sit: AI-114 has crept up from 2.1 mol% over the last half hour. TIC-107 is in AUTO and on its −97 °C set point; LIC-108 has come down a little.

0.1.unit: The feed gas (FIC-101, 42.2 t/h at 15 °C and 33 bar) is chilled in two steps before the demethanizer. E-101 cools it to −35 °C with boiling propylene (K-201 loop); V-101 separates the first liquid. E-102 cools the V-101 vapour to −97 °C with boiling ethylene (K-301 loop, PIC-301 suction about 1.14 bar a, ethylene boiling at −101 °C, TI-109). TIC-107 measures the gas leaving E-102 (TT-107) and sets the ethylene kettle level LIC-108: more level wets more tubes and gives more duty. V-102 (PIC-112, 32.5 bar a) separates the cold liquid (FI-111, feed 2 to the demethanizer) from the off-gas (FI-113, H2 and CH4 to fuel). AI-114 is the online GC on the off-gas: the ethylene in it is ethylene lost.

rows.what: Ethylene in the off-gas AI-114 has crept up from 2.1 mol% over the last half hour
AI-114 2.58 mol% against 2.12 at design; ethylene lost 368 kg/h against 283
TIC-107 in AUTO and on its −97 °C set point (PV -97.6 °C)
LIC-108 kettle level came down from 50 % to 41.6 % (its set point follows TIC-107)
Off-gas FI-113 up 3.75 → 4.29 t/h, cold liquid FI-111 down 19.98 → 19.34 t/h

0.4.ctx: Normal shift. No alarm on the console, no SIS action. Feed rate, feed temperature and V-102 pressure are on design. Nobody has touched TIC-107, LIC-108 or the ethylene compressor K-301. The case was run for 30 minutes without any action before the data was pulled.

R.1.p: V-102 is a flash drum: at a fixed pressure (PIC-112) the ethylene left in the vapour is set by the temperature alone. Colder gas, less ethylene lost. The temperature is held by TIC-107, which does not move a valve: it moves the set point of LIC-108, the ethylene level in the E-102 kettle. More level wets more tubes, so U·A and the duty rise. The ethylene boils at the temperature set by the K-301 suction pressure (PIC-301), about −101 °C. Every kilogram that boils goes to K-301, so FI-304 and JI-308 measure the E-102 duty.

R.2.eq: Q = U·A_wet(L)·ΔT_lm = m_C2=·λ ;   y_C2H4 = K(T, P)·x_C2H4

sym.m: E-102 duty; the boiling side equals the gas side
Tube area under the boiling ethylene; rises with the LIC-108 level
Ethylene boiled = K-301 suction flow FI-304
Latent heat of ethylene at −101 °C (≈ 480 kJ/kg)
Ethylene in the V-102 vapour = AI-114
Equilibrium ratio; falls steeply as T falls at fixed P

1.4.park: Not needed. Stop line: AI-114 above 3.5 mol% or any K-301 alarm → put TIC-107 in MAN and hold LIC-108 at 50 %.

1.5.sp: A reduced, stable condition that stops the problem growing while you investigate.

1.6.p: At a fixed V-102 pressure, the ethylene in the off-gas is set by the true V-102 temperature (flash equilibrium). AI-114 and TI-107 must agree.

3.2.n: Flash of the V-101 vapour at PI-112 32.49 bar a: AI-114 2.58 mol% needs the drum at -93.7 °C. TI-107 says -97.6 °C, so the gas is about 3.9 °C warmer than TT-107 reads. At −97 °C the same flash gives 2.12 mol%, the design value: the feed has not changed. FI-304 is 35.94 t/h against 37.69: less ethylene boils, so the duty really fell.

rows.c: Closes; the extra off-gas equals the lost liquid
Less duty with the same feed must give a WARMER outlet, yet TI-107 sits on −97

3.5.tree:
TOP: More ethylene in the off-gas with TIC-107 on set point
 OR — The drum is truly at −97 °C but loses more ethylene
    OR — Feed heavier (FI-101 / feed composition)
    OR — V-102 pressure low (PIC-112)
    OR — AI-114 reads high (analyser)
 OR — The drum is warmer than TI-107 says
    OR — TT-107 reads low (drift)
    OR — TIC-107 / LIC-108 cascade not doing its job
 OR — E-102 cannot give the duty
    OR — Surface lost (fouling, oil)
    OR — Ethylene side warm (PIC-301 high, non-condensables)
3.5.cut: Flash check and lab cut the first branch; low level with low duty cuts "surface lost"; TI-109 / PI-301 on design and the V-302 sample cut "ethylene side warm".

rows.st: “TIC-107 is on its set point, so the temperature is fine.”
rows.how: Only if TT-107 is right — the flash and the duty both say the gas is warmer
Checked and wrong: at −97 °C the flash of today’s V-101 vapour gives 2.12 mol%, the design value

3.8.n: No operator change. What drifts slowly and silently is an instrument: a temperature transmitter that loses calibration makes the controller hold the wrong temperature with no alarm. That fits a smooth 30-minute drift that started without any event in the log.

3.10.n: Team agrees: two independent numbers (AI-114 by the flash, FI-304 by the duty) disagree with TI-107; the lab clears AI-114.

3.11.n: Explore confirmed the numbers in 2.11; nothing contradicts it.

Feed richer in ethylene / heavier
V-102 pressure low

5.1.proof: Flash: AI-114 2.58 mol% means -93.7 °C, not -97.6; lab confirms AI-114; FI-304 down with LI-108 down; T-3: SP −2 °C → AI-114 2.63 → 2.45 mol%, LI-108 41.3 → 43.3 %
5.1.mech: TT-107 drifted to read about 4 °C low. TIC-107 sees −97 °C and is satisfied while the gas is really about −93.6 °C. Its output is the LIC-108 set point, so it has no reason to raise the level; as the error grew, it pulled the level DOWN (the reading looked a little too cold). Less wetted area → less ethylene boiled (FI-304, JI-308 down) → warmer V-102 → more ethylene stays in the vapour (AI-114, FI-113 up; FI-111 down).

rows.opt: Lower the TIC-107 set point by 4 °C (to −101 °C) until TT-107 is recalibrated; log it as a temporary set-point offset
Recalibrate TT-107 against a reference probe and return the set point to −97 °C
Add a consistency alarm: TI-107 vs the V-102 temperature implied by AI-114 and PI-112 (difference > 2 °C)
Second temperature element on the E-102 outlet (TT-107B) with deviation alarm

rows.step: TIC-107 SP −99 → −101 °C (4 °C below −97, the error found by the flash)
Shelve the TI-107 LO alarm while the offset is in place (it will read −101 °C); record it in the shelving log
If AI-114 does not fall below 2.4 mol% in 15 min, put the SP back to −97 °C and re-open Explore
Instrument technician checks TT-107 against a reference probe and recalibrates; SP back to −97 °C at once
Tell the demethanizer operator that feed 2 returns to normal

rows.act: TT-107 recalibrated; TIC-107 SP back to −97 °C

5.7.n: Directions all as predicted. After 20 min at −101 °C: AI-114 2.20 mol%, loss 296 kg/h, LI-108 47.8 %, FI-304 37.41 t/h — close to, but not at, design (2.12 / 283). Two reasons, both seen on the trend: TIC-107 is slow (integral time 300 s, through the level), and TI-107 read -100.4 °C, not −101, so the true gas was ≈ −96.4 °C. The TI-107 LO alarm came in at 00:51 — the predicted nuisance, shelved under 5.4. After the recalibration TI-107 reads true (-96.4 °C) and after 20 min AI-114 is 2.21 mol%, loss 295 kg/h: target 2.5 met (≤ 2.2 mol% at the rounding, ≤ 300 kg/h).

5.8.rule: If a controller sits on its set point but the variable it should hold (here AI-114 through the flash, or the duty FI-304) says otherwise, suspect the transmitter: check it against an independent number before you move anything else.

6.0.n: The flash and T-3 predicted the size of the error (≈ 4 °C) and the response. The set-point offset worked; the recalibration removed the cause. The only surprise was how slowly the cascade recovers — a timing lesson, not a wrong cause.

rows.m: Consistency alarm: TI-107 against the temperature implied by AI-114 and PI-112 (> 2 °C for 10 min)
Second element TT-107B on the E-102 outlet with a deviation alarm
TT-107 in the critical-instrument calibration list (6-monthly)
Shift round: compare AI-114 with the design curve at the TI-107 reading

6.1.kpi: Ethylene lost (kg/h) and the TI-107 − T(AI-114) difference, trended per shift

rows.i: ≈ USD 60/h of ethylene recovered to product
A known way to catch transmitter drift on this unit (flash check)
TI-107 LO nuisance alarm while the set-point offset was in place (shelved and logged)
K-301 power up 2.74 → 2.92 MW as the duty returns (expected: this is the duty the plant should carry)

hz.cause: Offset left in after the recalibration
hz.cons: Gas colder than needed; more K-301 power; heavier ends in feed 2
hz.sg: MOC record with an expiry; recalibration step returns the SP at once

6.3.fut: Before any set-point offset for a suspected transmitter, write the expiry and the person who removes it.

6.4.how: Found in one shift instead of a week of drift: ≈ 86 kg/h × 168 h ≈ 14 t of ethylene × USD 700/t ≈ USD 10 000 (OTS prices: ethylene USD 1 000/t, fuel USD 300/t).

6.5.again:
Check a controller PV against an independent number (composition by the flash, duty by the compressor flow) before moving anything.
Use the mass balance first: it showed the loss was real, not the analyser.
A small, reversible set-point test proved the cause in 10 minutes.
6.5.never: Never conclude “the temperature is fine” because the controller is on its set point.

evidence.text: AI-114 reads 2.58 mol% against its design value 2.12 mol% (+0.47).
LI-108 reads 41.6 % against its design value 50.0 % (-8.4).
FI-304 reads 35.94 t/h against its design value 37.69 t/h (-1.75); JI-308 2.74 MW (design 2.89).
FI-113 off-gas 4.29 t/h (design 3.75); FI-111 liquid 19.34 t/h (design 19.98).
TI-107 reads -97.6 °C, on its −97 °C set point (TIC-107 AUTO).
TI-109 -101.1 °C and PI-301 1.14 bar a on design: the ethylene boils at its design temperature.
PI-112 32.49 bar a and FI-101 42.18 t/h on design.
No alarm and no operator action in the log during the 30 minutes.
LIC-108 set point pulled down by TIC-107 from 50 % to 41.6 % — a smooth drift from 00:00.
Lab: off-gas 2.63 mol% C2H4 (AI-114 2.62 at the same time); V-302 vapour 100 % ethylene; water < 5 ppm.
Flash at PI-112: AI-114 2.58 mol% means -93.7 °C in V-102; TI-107 says -97.6 °C. At −97 °C the flash gives 2.12 mol%.
Mass balance V-101/V-102 closes within 0.4 %: the extra off-gas equals the lost liquid.
Fix: SP −101 °C, 20 min → AI-114 2.20 mol%, loss 296 kg/h; TI-107 LO alarm at 00:51.
After recalibration and SP −97 °C, 20 min → AI-114 2.21 mol%, loss 295 kg/h, TI-107 -96.4 °C.
